low_resolution_description: At low magnification, adenocarcinoma typically appears as irregular, infiltrative glandular structures with variable size and shape, often disrupting normal tissue architecture. Tumor regions may show cribriform patterns, necrosis, and desmoplastic stroma.
high_resolution_description: At high magnification, adenocarcinoma cells display enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with prominent nucleoli and increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio. Frequent mitoses and nuclear atypia are observed. Glandular lumens may contain mucin or necrotic debris.

low_resolution_description: At low magnification, non-adenocarcinoma tissue maintains well-organized, uniform glandular or ductal structures with preserved architecture. The stroma appears unremarkable, and no significant necrosis or abnormal growth patterns are seen.
high_resolution_description: At high magnification, non-adenocarcinoma cells exhibit uniform, small nuclei with fine chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli. The nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio is balanced, and mitotic figures are rare. Glandular lumens are clean and well-formed.
